quizName: DMV Practice Test #10 30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: If your front wheel locks while braking, what should you do?

options.text: Keep the tire locked until you stop completely.
Keep squeezing the front brake lever.
Release the front brake, then apply it again gently.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the front brake, then apply it again gently.
questions.explanation: If your front wheel locks while braking, release the brake pressure immediately. Then apply the brake again with slow, controlled pressure.

questions.question: What color are service signs?
questions.explanation: Blue signs with white letters show where services are located. These include rest areas, gas stations, restaurants, and hospitals.

questions.question: A motorcycle's brake light is _________ a car's brake light.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle's brake light is usually harder to see than a car's brake light, especially when the tail light is on. Other drivers may not notice your brake light.

questions.question: For an eye or face shield to work well, it must:

options.text: Limit side vision so you focus on the road ahead.
Not allow eyeglasses or sunglasses to be worn.

questions.explanation: An effective eye or face shield must have no scratches, resist penetration, allow clear side vision, fasten securely, allow air to prevent fogging, and allow room for eyeglasses or sunglasses if needed.

questions.question: Why should a motorcyclist not rely only on mirrors?

options.text: Mirrors can get dirty and limit your view.

questions.explanation: You cannot rely only on mirrors to know what is around you. Motorcycles have blind spots like any other vehicle.

questions.question: If you get a flat tire while riding, what should you do?

options.text: Hold the handlebars firmly and avoid using the brakes.
Shift your weight to the good wheel and brake normally.
Brake on the good wheel and pull off the road immediately.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the handlebars firmly and avoid using the brakes.
questions.explanation: If a tire goes flat while riding, grip the handlebars firmly and keep the motorcycle going straight. Only brake if you know which tire is flat. Slow down before leaving the road.

questions.question: What is the best way to help others see your motorcycle during normal riding?

options.text: Keep your high beam headlight on.
Paint your motorcycle a dark color.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your high beam headlight on.
questions.explanation: The best way for others to see your motorcycle is to use your headlight on high beam during the day and night when it is legal and safe to do so. Use running lights too if available.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs are white with red and black markings. They tell drivers about traffic laws in that area. This sign means right turns are not allowed.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They tell drivers about upcoming road conditions. This sign warns that a stop sign is ahead.

questions.question: As you approach a blind intersection, where should you position your motorcycle in the lane?

options.text: In the position that makes it easiest for other drivers to see you.
Closest to the traffic control device.
At the outside edge of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the position that makes it easiest for other drivers to see you.
questions.explanation: At a blind intersection, move to the part of the lane where other drivers can see you as soon as possible.

questions.question: You are most likely to get into a collision:
questions.explanation: Intersections have the most conflicts between you and other traffic.

questions.question: You have a better chance of surviving a crash if you wear:
questions.explanation: A helmet that meets DOT and state standards gives you the best head and neck protection. Wearing a good-quality, properly secured helmet is the single best way to survive a crash.

questions.question: When riding behind another vehicle at night, you can tell if there are bumps ahead by:

options.text: Listening for the other vehicle scraping the road.
Watching the other vehicle's taillights bounce up and down.
Looking at whether the rear bumper is bouncing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watching the other vehicle's taillights bounce up and down.
questions.explanation: Watch the vehicle ahead of you to see road conditions at night. If its taillights bounce up and down, bumps are coming.

questions.question: When motorcyclists ride in a group:

options.text: Inexperienced riders should lead the group.
Inexperienced riders should be near the front of the group.
Inexperienced riders should be at the back of the group.

questions.correctAnswerText: Inexperienced riders should be near the front of the group.
questions.explanation: Less experienced riders should ride near the front, behind the leader. This way, experienced riders can lead and watch the inexperienced riders at the same time.

questions.question: Hearing protection is:
questions.explanation: Wind and engine noise can damage your hearing over time, even with a helmet. Use hearing protection every time you ride.

questions.question: To control a motorcycle properly, you should:

options.text: Let your feet hang off the footrests.
Use your arms to hold up your body.
Keep your knees against the gas tank.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your knees against the gas tank.
questions.explanation: Sit with your arms slightly bent. Use your arms to steer, not to support yourself. Keep your knees against the gas tank to help balance during turns.

questions.question: Since most crashes happen in daylight, you:

options.text: Do not need to wear bright clothing during the day.
Should wear bright clothing during the day.
Should wear dark clothing during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should wear bright clothing during the day.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen in daylight. Wear bright-colored clothing to make yourself more visible when riding.

questions.question: When parked on the road, a motorcycle should:

options.text: Make an angle with the curb between 45 and 90 degrees.
Be parked without any wheel or fender touching the curb.
Be parked parallel to the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make an angle with the curb between 45 and 90 degrees.
questions.explanation: Park your motorcycle at an angle between 45 and 90 degrees to the curb. A wheel or fender should touch the curb.

questions.question: When starting your motorcycle, the engine should be in:
questions.explanation: The transmission must be in neutral before starting the engine. Most motorcycles have a neutral light on the speedometer that shows when the bike is in neutral.

questions.question: When changing lanes:

options.text: Your mirrors show you everything around you.
Turn your head to check blind spots in addition to using mirrors.
Signal and immediately move left or right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head to check blind spots in addition to using mirrors.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots like other vehicles. Always turn your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes, even if you use your mirrors.

questions.question: When choosing a helmet, you should ensure that it:
questions.explanation: A good helmet meets DOT and state safety standards. It should fit snugly all the way around with no cracks, loose padding, or frayed straps.

questions.question: Which of the following is not protective clothing?
questions.explanation: A leather jacket, denim pants, and full-fingered gloves protect you in a fall. Wear lace-up boots, high-top boots, or heavy shoes with ankle support instead of athletic shoes.

questions.question: Locking your brakes can:
questions.explanation: Locking your brakes causes control problems. If your front brake locks, release it and reapply it. If you lock your rear brake on dry pavement, keep it locked until you stop.

questions.question: When it starts to rain, it is usually best to:

options.text: Ride on the right side of the lane.
Ride on the edge of the road.
Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: When it first rains, the road becomes very slippery. Rainwater mixes with oil left by other cars. Ride in the tire tracks left by cars ahead of you for better grip.

questions.question: If a motorcycle rider takes a turn too fast, they may:

options.text: Have increased control of their motorcycle.

questions.explanation: Taking a turn too fast causes you to lose control. Your motorcycle may cross into another lane or go off the road.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. This sign warns you that the right lane ends ahead.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a potential problem?

options.text: An upcoming change in road surface characteristics
Conditions that do not appear to change as you approach

questions.correctAnswerText: Conditions that do not appear to change as you approach
questions.explanation: Look ahead for potential problems on the road and make a plan to stay safe.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a factor in determining blood alcohol content (BAC)?

options.text: How quickly the alcohol is consumed
How often the person consumes alcohol

questions.correctAnswerText: How often the person consumes alcohol
questions.explanation: BAC depends on body weight, how much alcohol you drink, and how fast you drink it. Never ride after drinking any amount of alcohol.

questions.question: When alcohol and drugs are consumed together, the effects:

options.text: Are less dangerous than when either is consumed alone.
Can be more pronounced than when either is consumed alone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can be more pronounced than when either is consumed alone.
questions.explanation: Many drugs, including prescription and over-the-counter medicines, can impair your riding. Mixing drugs with alcohol makes the danger even greater.

questions.question: To safely cross railroad tracks that are angled across your lane, you should:

options.text: Turn your motorcycle to take them at a 90-degree angle.

questions.explanation: Ride straight through your lane when crossing angled railroad tracks. Turning your motorcycle can send you into another lane and is dangerous.
